summary: Blind tournament over anonymous A-D, viewed in order D, B, A, C with each scored alone on all nine OPERATE dimensions before comparison, names A the winner on the class priorities (task clarity, state completeness, predictable interaction) with C taking visual strength and scalability, D implementation risk, and B last on states. The verdict for A is repairable, not approve: its CSS hides tool-status labels at 375px against its own status-never-color-only absolute and adopted floor C-A2, and its docked-composer claim is never pinned. One hybrid move is recommended (import C turn-header status rollup plus keep-status/hide-duration rule into A ticket head), and a packet-level blindness leak (specimens embed direction names in-page) is flagged for the Coordinator.

claims.claim: A shows the widest in-context state vocabulary: failed-in-place with retry and dismiss-with-reason, staged running with queued step and honest stub labels, declared empty-trace turn, per-session wing with empty view, all five tool kinds.

A hides tool-row status labels and durations at max-width:480px, so collapsed rows at 375px carry no status label, violating its own status-never-color-only absolute and adopted floor C-A2 at a required viewport.
B has computed AA failures (faint caps about 3.5:1, running status about 4.1:1) and renders only the Files verification view; Browser and GitHub tabs are empty.

C is the only specimen with a genuinely pinned sticky-bottom composer, documented AA-passing status color pairings, and state-aware follow-ups; its evidence-wing anomaly auto-promotion is the least predictable interaction in the field.

D stacks the resumption ledger above the conversation at 700px, contradicting its own note, and never pins the composer despite claiming it always reachable; its specimens embed direction names and theses in-page (as do all four), a blindness leak for the Coordinator to rule on.

Overall winner A, decided on OPERATE priorities (task clarity, state completeness, predictable interaction) after a 2-2 A/C criterion tie; trade-offs accepted: C superior craft and a11y polish, B/D distinctiveness, A higher build complexity (spine scrollspy).

risks: A hides tool-row status labels at 480px; unfixed it violates C-A2 at a required viewport; fix is one CSS line (keep status, hide duration).
A 52px numerals compete with prose in 30-plus turn sessions; no collapse rule for settled tickets.
A runs two parallel color systems (kind chips vs status pills) that will drift as the system grows.
A spine scroll-sync asserted but static; composer docked claim never pinned in CSS; both must become real in the build.
All four specimens make responsive claims their CSS only partially proves; build needs a rendered 375/768/1440 verification pass.
Run-level: specimens self-identify direction names and theses in-page, weakening the blind; Coordinator must rule whether this verdict counts as fully independent Evidence.
unresolved: No rendered 375/768/1440 views accompany any candidate; a live 375px pass of A, C, D would settle severity ranking and could promote A hidden status labels to a blocker.
Focus management unverifiable from markup: B sheet has no focus trap; A/C drawer overlays are labels without implemented behavior.
Motion judged from code only; rendered-motion review pending.
Coordinator ruling required on the in-page direction-name leak before the verdict counts as fully independent Evidence.
Second critic winner unknown by design; material disagreement needs Coordinator reconciliation.
